title: Foundations of the Human Body
welcome_lead: Step into the human body and meet the systems that keep an athlete moving, breathing and beating with life.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Anatomy & Physiology foundations: skeletal functions, muscle types, respiratory and cardiovascular basics.
final_note: Brilliant! You have built a strong foundation in the body systems that power sport.

concepts.def: Framework of 206 bones giving the body shape and support.
Involuntary muscle found only in the heart wall.
Skeletal muscle under conscious control for movement.
Involuntary muscle in walls of organs like the gut.
Tiny air sacs in lungs where gas exchange happens.
Tiny vessels, one cell thick, for gas and nutrient exchange.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The skeleton has five key functions for sport and life:

  • Support — keeps you upright.
  • Protection — skull guards the brain, ribs guard the lungs and heart.
  • Movement — bones act as levers for muscles to pull on.
  • Blood cell production — red and white cells form in bone marrow.
  • Mineral storage — stores calcium and phosphorus.

The body has three muscle types: cardiac (heart only, involuntary), smooth (organs, involuntary) and voluntary skeletal (attached to bones, under conscious control). Only voluntary skeletal muscle moves you during sport.
Air travels down the trachea, into bronchi, then bronchioles and finally into alveoli. Oxygen diffuses across the thin alveolar wall into capillaries, while carbon dioxide diffuses out to be exhaled.
